item.title: Judge says Trump can't demolish Kennedy Center. And, lawsuits target voter intimidation
item.description:

item.title: Bolivia: New cat species discovered by scientists
item.description:
Fernando Faciole/National Geogra / Fernando Faciole, Reuters Researchers say they’ve discovered a new wild cat species, previously unknown to science. The cat, named Leopardus tilcayo, is smaller than the average house cat, is slender, spotted and has rounded ears. The new species, which was first announced in the journal Current Biology on Thursday, is native to the Bolivian Yungas, the cloud forest where the Andes Mountains intersect with the Amazon basin. “This time, it’s a cat. That’s really novel. And it hasn’t happened in 100 years,” said Paola Nogales-Ascarrunz, who co-authored the study and leads a wild cat conservation program in Bolivia. “No one else had named it. No one else had described it.” She says it’s rare to identify a new, relatively large mammal. Compared to some other animals, Leopardus tilcayo may be big, but Nogales-Ascarrunz says she was initially struck by its…

item.title: Climate change made deadly Nepal glacier and rock collapse more likely, analysis finds
item.description:
Scientists say global heating was a destabilising factor in collapse of 200,000 sq metre glacier in August Climate breakdown probably weakened the glacier that collapsed causing catastrophic floods and killing over a thousand people in Nepal and Tibet last month, the first scientific study of the disaster has found. Researchers identified unusually warm conditions before the glacier’s collapse , which sent an avalanche of 110m cubic metres (3.885bn cu ft) of snow and ice into the valley below. This triggered flash floods on an almost unprecedented scale, hitting communities downstream without warning. Continue reading...

item.title: Russia votes in parliamentary election as war in Ukraine drags on
item.description:
Russian State Duma elections began Friday — the first since the invasion of Ukraine in 2022 — including in its occupied areas there, where Russia will look to reinforce the illusion of popular support for its full-scale invasion and annexation of eastern Ukraine. OSCE election observers are not invited to monitor the outcome of the elections, a telling signal, critics say, that the Kremlin has no intentions of conducting free and fair elections. "Russia’s refusal to invite an election observation mission seriously breaches its international commitments and shows a worrying disregard for democratic standards. Election observation is not optional — it is something that all OSCE participating States have agreed to, and it is a cornerstone of transparency and accountability," OSCE Parliamentary Assembly President Pere Joan Pons told Fox News Digital. item.title: Thomas and Alito Are More Reliable Votes for Trump Than His Own Supreme Court Appointees
item.description:
President Donald Trump dramatically reshaped the U.S. Supreme Court during his first term by appointing three new justices who then made possible a series of far-reaching decisions beloved by legal conservatives, including the narrowing of the reach of the Voting Rights Act and the total elimination of the constitutional right to abortion. But none of that means that Trump actually looks fondly upon the Court that he has so thoroughly remade. "This Supreme Court is bullied and cajoled by the Radical Left," he recently fumed on social media, "into making decisions that have set America back at least a hundred years." Trump is upset for a simple reason: While the conservative legal movement has been winning big at the Court, Trump's own record is rather more mixed. item.title: US approves $24.3 billion sale of 48 F-35 warplanes to Saudi Arabia
item.description:
The State Department’s approval of the proposed $24.3 billion sale of 48 Lockheed Martin F-35 fighter jets to Saudi Arabia represents a major victory for the kingdom, as Riyadh seeks US support amid increased attacks from Iran-backed groups. The sale must still undergo congressional review, where it will likely face opposition. The announcement comes nearly two months after Saudi Defense Minister Khalid bin Salman traveled to Washington to lobby senior Trump administration officials on the sale, with Riyadh hoping to advance the deal ahead of the midterms. Earlier this month, the administration announced a separate conventional arms sale to Saudi Arabia. On Thursday, Sens. Ed Markey, D-Mass., and Jeff Merkley, D-Ore., introduced a joint resolution of disapproval targeting that proposed sale.
